clue.text: Humour eliciting irate response?

blocks.note: first meaning: a mood or frame of mind, as in good humour
second meaning: an outburst of anger

explanation.surface: A joke that makes someone cross instead of making them laugh.
explanation.walkthrough: Humour here is the old sense of mood or disposition, not comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a person's mood or disposition and a fit of anger, as in losing it.

clue.text: Entrance for lorries?

blocks.note: first meaning: rapture, read as en-TRANCE, to delight
second meaning: vehicles that carry goods (a lorry is a truck)

explanation.surface: A gateway or way in meant for trucks.
explanation.walkthrough: Entrance looks like a noun meaning a way in; it is the verb to enrapture, and lorries stand for the whole business of carrying goods.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrapture someone is to carry them away with delight, and road vehicles moving goods are collectively a carrying system.

clue.text: Girl, moreover, has no end of books

indicators.note: having no end means the final letter of the preceding word is lopped off

blocks.note: a young unmarried woman
a synonym, meaning in addition

explanation.surface: A girl who also owns some books, lacking an ending.
explanation.definitionFit: Missals are the liturgical volumes containing the order of Mass for the year.

clue.text: Adults generally choose to speak out

blocks.note: to pick, especially by voting
to make a formal speech

explanation.surface: Grown-ups as a rule decide to voice their opinions.
explanation.definitionFit: The voters of a country are, broadly speaking, its grown-up population, since the franchise begins at adulthood.

clue.text: The other side of the coin, so to speak

definitions.text: The other side of the coin

blocks.clueFragment: The other side of the coin
blocks.note: first meaning: the opposite or reverse of a statement
second meaning: to talk with someone

explanation.surface: An idiom for the opposite view, followed by the tag 'so to speak'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So to speak' reads as a stock phrase apologising for the idiom, but its last word is a second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it is the opposite proposition, and as a verb it means to hold a conversation.

clue.text: Arranged for a design or model

indicators.note: to model is to shape or mould material into a new form

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something set out to serve as a design or a model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' looks like a noun paired with design; it is a verb telling you to reshape the three words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Arranged and this word both describe things put into a neat, planned order.

clue.text: Struggle over Welsh capital survey

indicators.note: a capital is the letter at the head of a word, so only its opening is kept

blocks.note: to compete or contend
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A battle fought over Cardiff, followed by an inspection.
explanation.walkthrough: Welsh capital suggests Cardiff, but it is just the capital letter of Welsh. In a down clue, 'over' simply places the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: To survey a scene is to look at it as a whole, which is the verb's sense here.

clue.text: Gnarled root -- it's used as food

indicators.note: gnarled means twisted and knotted out of its natural shape

blocks.note: taken as written, ignoring the dash and apostrophe

explanation.surface: A knotty root being put to use as something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an Italian dish of rice cooked slowly in stock, so a kind of meal.

clue.text: Within a year Lydia may be dead -- so soon

indicators.note: within says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

blocks.note: the letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A grim prediction that Lydia could die within twelve months, which seems too soon.
explanation.walkthrough: Most of the clue is scene-setting; the answer spans the gap between the two words after 'Within a'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean before the expected or usual time.

clue.text: Drop the rent

blocks.note: first meaning: a single bead of water from the eye
second meaning: a rip in fabric

explanation.surface: An order to stop paying, or lower, the rent.
explanation.walkthrough: Rent looks like money paid to a landlord; it is a split or rip.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun covers a droplet shed when crying and, pronounced differently, a split in cloth.

clue.text: Cold continent

blocks.note: first meaning: stern and unfriendly in manner
second meaning: self-restrained, abstaining from pleasures

explanation.walkthrough: Cold continent suggests Antarctica; continent is the adjective meaning self-restrained.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes a severe, unwelcoming manner and an ascetic life of strict self-denial.

clue.text: A man like Uriah Heep possibly agrees with the Right

indicators.note: possibly suggests the following word is only one of its possible arrangements

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A Dickensian toady sides with the political right.
explanation.walkthrough: Uriah Heep is the fawning, 'ever so 'umble' clerk in Dickens's David Copperfield.
explanation.definitionFit: A greaser is a flatterer who oils his way into favour, exactly Heep's character type.

clue.text: Give voice about a mad character cracking up

indicators.note: about means going around something, so one word wraps the other

blocks.note: to use the voice musically
the Mad Hatter from Alice in Wonderland

explanation.surface: Someone talking about an insane person who is having a breakdown.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe something breaking into pieces, and figuratively someone falling apart emotionally.

clue.text: Suspension from a rope

blocks.note: first meaning: a postponement
second meaning: a rope supporting a ship's mast

explanation.surface: Something hanging on the end of a line.
explanation.walkthrough: Suspension suggests hanging from the rope; it means a legal postponement.
explanation.definitionFit: A court can grant a delay of proceedings, and on a sailing ship a supporting cable for the mast has the same name.

clue.text: Agent about to advance one five hundred pounds in a grand manner

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word goes round the rest

blocks.note: a secret agent
to advance money is to lend it
Roman numeral one
Roman numeral five hundred
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: A bank agent about to lend someone five hundred pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' reads as 'on the point of'; split it so that about is the wrapper and to is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means magnificently or lavishly, which is acting in a grand style.

clue.text: 6, say

blocks.note: first meaning: the answer to 6 down, to look at
second meaning: to remark

explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like it means 'for example', but it is a second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to watch or notice and to make a comment, as in 'he observed that it was late'.

clue.text: The Spanish tale men spin of the power of nature

indicators.note: to spin is to turn round, so the letters come out in a new order

blocks.note: el is the Spanish word for the
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Spanish legend that men tell about nature's forces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spin' suggests telling a yarn, which fits tale, but it signals rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to the primal forces of earth, air, fire and water.

clue.text: Drink left for 13

blocks.note: to sip or drink
port is the left-hand side of a ship

explanation.surface: A drink to take away, ordered for thirteen people.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 refers to the answer at 13 across, a prop or brace.
explanation.definitionFit: A stay is a prop or brace that holds something up, the same idea as a supporting strut.

clue.text: Note obvious embarrassment and fatigue

blocks.note: the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
a blush is embarrassment that shows

explanation.surface: Remarking on someone's blushing and weariness.
explanation.definitionFit: Fatigue and this noun are synonyms for exhaustion, the state of needing sleep.

clue.text: The boards should get the rate adjusted

indicators.note: something adjusted has been altered and set differently

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A company board insisting that a price should be changed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The boards' suggests directors; it is the stage, as in treading the boards.
explanation.definitionFit: The boards is an idiom for the stage and so for the acting profession and drama generally.

clue.text: Sees foreign cash is offensive to 6

definitions.note: a phrase; the answer is a noun for a thing that is offensive to view

blocks.note: to eye is to look at
the öre is a small coin of Sweden, Denmark and Norway

explanation.surface: Someone notices foreign money and finds it distasteful.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 is the answer at 6 down, to look at.
explanation.definitionFit: An ugly building or object is called this because it pains whoever has to look at it.

clue.text: She'll provide Shylock, for example, with change

definitions.text: She'll provide Shylock, for example, with change

blocks.clueFragment: She'll provide Shylock, for example, with change
blocks.note: surface reading: someone giving the moneylender of The Merchant of Venice small coins
setter's reading: Shylock is a stage role, and the change is a change of costume put on the actor backstage

explanation.surface: A woman giving the moneylender Shylock some loose coins.
explanation.walkthrough: Shylock is the famous moneylender, so change suggests money; he is a stage part, and change is a costume change.
explanation.definitionFit: In the theatre this person helps actors into their costumes and handles quick changes between scenes.

clue.text: Less reputable publicity -- and more nervous about it

indicators.note: being about it means wrapped around the preceding item

blocks.note: comparative of shy
short for advertisement

explanation.surface: Sleazier advertising, and someone growing more anxious over it.
explanation.definitionFit: Shady means of dubious honesty, so the comparative means more disreputable.

clue.text: Bound to be drawn

blocks.note: first meaning: fastened with rope
second meaning: finishing level in a game

explanation.surface: Certain to be pulled out, as in a raffle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to be' reads as 'certain to be'; split it into two definitions with 'to be' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means fastened with knots and also level on scores at the end of a match.

clue.text: Imperial Chinese would accept a point that's sound

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so one piece is placed inside the other

blocks.note: the Tang dynasty ruled China from 618 to 907
a point of the compass, west

explanation.surface: A Chinese emperor would agree to a sound argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective meaning valid; it is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A twang is a ringing, plucked noise, or a nasal accent, so a kind of sound.

clue.text: 17 worker on the watch

blocks.note: 17 across is support; to back a motion is to second it
a farm or factory labourer

explanation.surface: A supporting worker keeping watch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the watch' suggests being on guard; it is a watch face.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the pointer on a timepiece that sweeps round once a minute, so it is literally found on a wristwatch.

clue.text: No longer writing about the church

blocks.note: a book on a topic is writing about it
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone has stopped writing about religion.
explanation.walkthrough: CE, the Church of England, is a standard abbreviation for the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Formerly is the shared sense: what was the case at some past time but is not now.

clue.text: Pen name

blocks.note: surface reading: a pseudonym used by an author
setter's reading: to pen one's name, that is to write it in one's own hand on a document

explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen name' is a stock noun for a pseudonym; read pen as a verb and it means to write your name.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing your name at the foot of a letter or cheque is exactly this verb's meaning.

clue.text: An individual in love - or in a fog!

indicators.note: in says one piece goes inside the next

blocks.note: taken as written
a thin fog
taken as written

explanation.surface: Being in love feels like being in a haze.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash seems to split love from fog as alternatives; or is just two letters for the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a literary word for a lover or someone given to romance.

clue.text: Regulations in the Orient covering a certain drug

blocks.note: a body of rules
taken as written
E for east

explanation.surface: Eastern laws dealing with a particular narcotic.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an opiate painkiller derived from morphine, used in cough medicines.

clue.text: A pest both naive and knowing

blocks.note: inexperienced
fly is British slang for sharp or shrewd

explanation.surface: An annoying person who is somehow both innocent and worldly.
explanation.walkthrough: The contradiction is the joke: two opposite words give one insect.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the aphid, a tiny sap-sucking insect that gardeners treat as a plague on roses.

clue.text: Persian king keeping quiet in Mediterranean island

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the king surrounds the next letter

blocks.note: Cyrus the Great, founder of the Persian empire
p for piano, the musical direction for soft

explanation.surface: An ancient king living quietly on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the large island state in the eastern part of that sea, south of Turkey.
